justification: Copy-only. Removes the words 'and page' from three user-facing surfaces that claimed every control is cited to its clause AND page. The page half was disproven on production 2026-08-23 and corrected in ~/.claude/plans/ce-institutional-endorsement-gtm-2026-07.md the same day, but the correction was applied only to the outreach email draft - the product surfaces kept the claim. Re-measured on production today, 2026-08-23: of 967 current, not-needs-review rows in dcp_setback_controls, 779 (80.6%) carry no pdf_page; excluding nsw_statewide and the all-dead inner_west label, 748 of 936 served rows (79.9%) carry no page. The clause half is true for every served row: section_ref and source_text are 100% filled (936/936). So the fix is to delete the false half and keep the true one. Direction of change is claim-removal, which per memory/project-defect-repair-calibration-2026-08.md cannot create a new false claim - it can only stop one. No logic, no data, no types touched: three JSX string literals. SECOND CHANGE on this branch: the pre-push liability scan flagged both sentences this branch had just edited, and it was correct. Each claimed every control/figure is traced to a published CLAUSE while listing sources that have none - Spatial Services NSW mapping, council flood studies, the RFS bushfire layer. The 936/936 section_ref measurement covers dcp_setback_controls only and says nothing about mapping results, so the claim was broader than the evidence. Both sentences now split the two: a planning control carries its clause, a mapping result names its dataset. Same direction of travel - narrowing a claim to the subset that was measured. THIRD CHANGE: an audit of all seven /for/ audience pages found five more claims of the same shape - a number from one layer of the coverage ladder attached to a capability from another. floodLgas:71 was documented as 'LGAs with modelled flood-depth coverage'; 71 is the flood OVERLAY council count (spatial_overlays layer_type='flood' -> 72) while services/flood_truth.py declares exactly FOUR council flood studies. lgasCovered:130 published more councils than NSW contains, on the homepage, in a file that already held totalNswCouncils:128. '25 LGAs' for front+side+rear setbacks: 24 councils hold all three. 'never a guess' and 'Always current' were absolutes that did not hold across the products they spanned. All fixed at the shared source lib/coverage.ts so every consumer moved at once - the blast radius was six surfaces for floodLgas, not one.

break_it.scenario: Someone reads this change as 'the page data was fixed' and re-states a page-level citation claim somewhere else.
break_it.what_happens: Nothing about the data changed. 748 of 936 served controls still carry no pdf_page, and effective_date_basis is still 0% filled. Only the promise moved. A later doc or deck saying 'cited to the page' would be exactly as false as the header was this morning.
break_it.how: NOT mitigated. This is a copy edit, not a data repair. The honest statement of the surface is: every served control carries its clause and its verbatim source sentence; roughly one in five also carries a page.
break_it.repro: SELECT count(*), count(pdf_page) FROM dcp_setback_controls WHERE is_current AND (needs_review IS NULL OR needs_review=FALSE) AND lga <> 'nsw_statewide' AND lga <> 'inner_west'

break_it.scenario: The phrase is re-introduced on a new surface, or restored on one of these three.
break_it.what_happens: It ships. No test, lint or CI job fails on it. This claim already survived one documented correction: it was corrected in the GTM plan file on 2026-08-23 and the product kept serving it, because a plan file cannot fail a build.
break_it.how: NOT mitigated, and this is the real residual risk in this change. Per memory/feedback-incident-rule-machine.md a prose rule fails within hours and only a gated rule holds. A standing lint on the phrase is the durable fix and is deliberately NOT bundled here.
break_it.repro: grep -rn 'clause and page' frontend-nextjs/app frontend-nextjs/components frontend-nextjs/lib | grep -v node_modules

break_it.scenario: Removing 'and page' hides the page numbers on the 188 rows that legitimately have one.
break_it.what_happens: It does not. Page rendering is conditional and independent of the header: ProvisionDisplay.tsx:232 renders the page span only when provision.pdfPage is truthy, so a page shows wherever one exists and nothing shows where it does not. The header was the only thing promising a page on every control.
break_it.how: Verified by reading the render path rather than assumed. The change aligns the header with behaviour the UI already had.

break_it.scenario: The two-line JSX text node in for/conveyancers/page.tsx breaks or reads wrong after the words are removed mid-sentence.
break_it.what_happens: It renders as '...traced to the published clause it comes from - zoning and SEPP from the NSW Planning Portal...'. Grammatical, and the source list after the em-dash is unchanged.
break_it.how: JSX text node, line break preserved; tsc ran clean at 8 errors against a 677 baseline.

break_it.scenario: A conveyancing report or widget result includes a flood, bushfire or hazard figure that came from mapping, not from a planning instrument.
break_it.what_happens: Before this branch's second commit both surfaces told the reader that figure was 'traced to the published clause it comes from'. No such clause exists for a Spatial Services mapping result or an RFS bushfire layer, so the sentence overstated provenance to a conveyancer - the reader least equipped to catch it and the one whose reliance carries liability.
break_it.how: Both sentences now distinguish the two provenance kinds explicitly: a planning control carries the clause it was read from, a mapping result names its dataset. This was found by the repo's own pre-push liability scan rather than by review, and the scan's two findings were accepted rather than annotated away.
break_it.repro: git show 13a6a68a --stat && grep -n 'names where it came from' frontend-nextjs/app/for/conveyancers/page.tsx

break_it.scenario: A published coverage number drifts from, or was never equal to, the thing it names.
break_it.what_happens: It ships and stays. scripts/verify_coverage_stats.py PASSED throughout this defect's life for two separate reasons: floodLgas and lgasCovered were classed 'editorial' and checked by NOTHING, and dcpNumericCouncils was validated against the SAME query that produces the omission it should catch. A guard whose shape looks right and which cannot fail on the live defect is the pattern in memory/feedback-detect-a-guard-by-forcing-its-failure.md.
break_it.how: Three checks added to the verifier and each FORCED TO FAIL on the exact historical wrong value before being trusted, not reasoned about: lgasCovered 130 -> DRIFT, dcpSetbackTripleCouncils 25 -> DRIFT, floodStudies 71 -> DRIFT. Plus a structural invariant that lgasCovered can never exceed totalNswCouncils. All four fire together and the script exits 1. Restored to correct values: all OK, exit 0. floodStudies is checked by parsing FLOOD_STUDIES out of services/flood_truth.py, so the published number is tied to the declaration rather than to an editor's memory.
break_it.repro: python -c "import io;p='frontend-nextjs/lib/coverage.ts';s=io.open(p,encoding='utf-8').read();io.open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s.replace('lgasCovered: 128','lgasCovered: 130'))" && python scripts/verify_coverage_stats.py; git checkout -- frontend-nextjs/lib/coverage.ts

break_it.scenario: A user in Tweed or Wollongong asks the flood question and expects the modelled depth the site advertises.
break_it.what_happens: They get 'not assessed'. Dockerfile.python sets HAWKESBURY_RASTER_DIR and REDBANK_RASTER_DIR but NOT the Tweed/Wollongong pair, and the two sides disagree on that env var's fallback: download_tweed_wollongong_rasters.py:66 defaults to /tmp/tweed_rasters while flood_truth.py defaults to data/flood_studies/tweed, which is untracked and never copied into the container. The rasters download on every boot into a directory nothing reads.
break_it.how: NOT mitigated, and deliberately out of scope for a copy change - it is a production deploy change. It is NOT a false negative: flood_study_raster_availability() is consulted per run and #892 guarantees 'not assessed' rather than 'no', and _warn_on_absent_flood_studies() logs at import. The copy was written to describe behaviour ('where a council flood study has been ingested') rather than to promise a count, so it stays true either way. Fix is two ENV lines matching the Hawkesbury/Redbank pattern already in that Dockerfile.

post_merge.db_reset: No. No database access of any kind - three string literals. The database was read only to measure the claim (read-only session, set_session readonly), never written.
post_merge.secrets: No credentials read or written by this change. Noted separately and NOT addressed here: the live Supabase pooler password remains in git history across ~96 tracked files per memory/project-live-db-password-in-git-history-2026-08.md. That still needs rotation and is untouched by this commit.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes. After deploy, open https://verify.plotdetect.com.au/assessment and confirm the header sub-line reads 'Every control cited to its clause - live NSW planning data' with no page claim. The pre-fix string was confirmed live in a browser on 2026-08-23, so a source-only check is not sufficient - the deployed bundle is the authority, per the method used in ce-verified-capability-statement-2026-08.md section 3.1.

not_covered: app/for/students/page.tsx already said 'Every control cited to its clause' and was correct before this change - left untouched.

app/api/adg/separation-table/route.ts carries an internal code comment referring to 'PDF URL and page number'. It describes sepp_adg_requirements, a different table, and is not user-facing. Not verified and not changed.
No standing lint or CI check was added. The phrase can return without failing anything.

The clause-fill measurement (936/936 section_ref) covers dcp_setback_controls only. No equivalent provenance-fill measurement was run for zoning, SEPP, flood, bushfire or hazard mapping results - the copy now claims only that those name a dataset, which is weaker and was not separately verified per-field.

Whether the R2 download in download_tweed_wollongong_rasters.py succeeds in production was not observed - only that its destination and flood_truth.py's lookup path cannot agree while the env vars are unset.

Six of coverage.ts's fifteen fields remain unchecked by the verifier: dcpFullCouncils, seppStandards, adgCriteria, secondaryDwellingCouncils, riskLayers, govDataSources. Three were added this branch; these six were not audited.
